text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Shares finished higher, the first day of the new British tax year, as FTSE 100 shadowed a firmer Wall Street. But continued worries about possible near-term U.S. and UK rate hikes were expected to put a cap on any FTSE advance. The FTSE 100 closed 35.1 points up at 4,271.7.

FRANKFURT - Shares continued their recovery after huge losses registered in the bearish slide of the previous week, with support coming from a firmer opening on Wall Street and a revival in the dollar's fortunes. The IBIS DAX index ended trade at 3,342.77 points, up 3.32 percent or 107.42 points. Earlier the DAX index, which tracks bourse trade, ended the day at 3,312.88 point, up 67.95 points or 2.09 percent.

PARIS - Shares closed sharply higher as sentiment changed as dramatically as the weather and Wall Street and the dollar surged ahead after last week's falls. The CAC-40 blue-chip index closed 54.34 points higher at 2,572.31, below the day's high of 2,589.11.

ZURICH - Shares jumped, with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index closing 2.6 percent on a correction after recent losses. Position squaring, gains in Swiss bond futures, a firmer tone on Wall Street and a firmer U.S. dollar also boosted Swiss share prices. The SMI of leading shares ended up 116.5 points, or 2.61 percent, at 4,588.0 points. The all-share SPI was up 66.62 points, or 2.35 percent, to 2,903.15.

TOKYO - Stocks ended lower, as afternoon selling in the financial and construction sectors erased early gains by exporters, whose shares were buoyed by the yen's weakening against the dollar. The Nikkei average fell 144.92 points or 0.81 percent to 17,715.67.

HONG KONG - Stocks edged upwards in thin trade to close firmer, despite lingering concern over the outlook for Wall Street and for interest rates. The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 83.25 points, or 0.68 percent, at 12,287.84. Turnover was HK$5.05 billion, marginally ahead of Friday's HK$4.91 billion.

SYDNEY - The share market drifted to close just lower as traders remained indecisive and uninterested ahead of further Wall Street moves and the much-awaited Wallis report into the financial system. The All Ordinaries index eased 3.5 points to 2,366.0.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks climbed in late afternoon trade, bolstered by robust foreign interest which pushed them to end near the day's best levels. Dealers said gains received further support from a strong showing on Wall Street on Friday, hopes of another rise on the Dow on Monday and local futures arbitrage activity. The industrial 100 percent index added 46.5 points to 8,285.6. The all-share index closed up 58.9 points at 7,074.7. The gold index ended up 16.4 points at 1,307.9.
